content:
alex: Heads up — after last night's canary we saw FP8 path on H100 regressions for long contexts. p99 spiked and throughput dropped.
ryan: Seen it. Traces show a lot of kernel-switch chatter around KV-cache warmup + microbatch merging.
jing: Pasting a short profiler excerpt I grabbed from the canary VM:
```
CPU: scheduler 18% -> 36%
GPU kernels: fp8_dot (hot) then repeated fallbacks to int8_slowpath
p50: 28ms, p95: 98ms, p99: 210ms (baseline p99 ~65ms)
```
alex: Key numbers — throughput ~ -18% on seq=2048 workload, p99 went 65ms -> 210ms. Scheduler CPU and context-switches also up.
maria: Are we sure it's FP8 kernels and not Transformer Engine (TE) config changes? We flipped some TE flags before the canary.
sam: Confirmed: TE flags in the canary image were `--te-online-tiling=on --quant-mode=fp8-adaptive --te-prefetch=1`.
devops-bot: deploy 3888879000 finished: canary traffic=5% (image: te-2026-03-17)
jing: Kernel logs show repeated fallback from `fp8_dot` -> `int8_slowpath` at runtime. Fallback reason: occasional NaN detection in accumulators during certain layers.
ryan: The NaN frequency correlates with large microbatch reuse and KV-stale eviction spikes. Looks like a KV alignment / warmup race coupled to batching heuristic.
maria: That fits a calibration-drift pattern. If per-op FP8 scales are computed on short warmups then merging microbatches can move activations out of calibrated range.
alex: Repro script I used: `./scripts/repro_longctx.sh --model gptx-13b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --fp8` — reproduces locally.
sam: I ran the repro and attached a flamegraph. Heat is concentrated in the kernel-selection dispatcher + a small hot loop where we check `is_finite` and fallback.
```
KERNEL_SELECT: layer12 q=fp8_dot -> int8_slowpath (reason=NaNDetected)
KV_EVICT: idx=12345 warmup=0.2ms
BATCHER: microbatch shape [1,512] -> merged [1,2048]
```
maria: Hypothesis: our batching heuristic merges microbatches aggressively causing per-op scale estimates to be unstable after merge. Suggest clamping scales for merged batches or delaying merge until scales are stable.
jing: Quick mitigations: force `quant-mode=fp8-legacy` for H100 canaries (this uses older stable quant codepath) and add detection to avoid merging across large scale shifts.
alex: Can we A/B? Route a subset of canary to `fp8-legacy` and another to `fp8-adaptive` with extra telemetry.
ryan: Also need to surface KV-cache miss/eviction heatmap — current metrics are too coarse. Missing eviction latency per-shard.
sam: Filed infra ticket INF-4321 to add per-shard KV eviction latency and `scale_update_count` telemetry.
devops-bot: infra ticket created: INF-4321 by sam
maria: Important: when fallback happens we not only lose throughput but we also see a small distribution shift in logits. Need eval harness run on canary prompts to check quality drift.
jing: I'll add `scale_update_count` and `last_scale_value` to per-request telemetry and attach them to canary traces.
alex: Short-term plan: roll back TE adaptive quant flag on prod canary (restore canary to `fp8-legacy`) to stop user impact. Long-term: implement batching-safe scale-merge + per-request calibration and better fallback backoff.
ryan: :thumbsup: I'll own the rollback and the A/B routing. Pushing PR now.
sam: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/te-config/pull/789 — updates default quant-mode for h100 images used in canaries.
alex: Thanks team. Schedule quick triage sync at 10:30 to decide next steps and assign follow-ups. Keep updates in this thread.
